message.body:
Rationale:
  - Add standards-based graph-only RDF ingestion without widening
    Turtle/N3 acceptance or bypassing the shared RDF-to-OWL
    reconstruction boundary.
  - Close Phase 12 with pinned W3C conformance evidence, Java
    differential coverage, browser integration, and measured performance
    evidence.

User Experience Changes:
  - WebVOWL can load N-Triples ontology documents directly and through
    import closure.
  - N-Quads and TriG remain intentionally unregistered and Turtle
    directives are rejected by the N-Triples parser.

File Changes:
 1. `docs/owlapi-js/README.md`
    - Publish N-Triples support, its strict format boundary, and the
      Phase 12 verification surface in the owlapi-js documentation entry
      point.
 2. `docs/owlapi-js/compatibility/capabilities.json`
    - Record N-Triples as a supported public syntax while retaining
      N-Quads and TriG as explicit unsupported boundaries.
 3. `docs/owlapi-js/conformance/classification-manifests.json`
    - Register the pinned RDF 1.1 and RDF 1.2 N-Triples manifests so
      conformance fixtures remain reproducible and reviewable.
 4. `docs/owlapi-js/conformance/generated/w3c-ntriples.json`
    - Materialize the classified 99-case W3C N-Triples corpus used by
      the executable positive and negative conformance tests.
 5. `docs/owlapi-js/conformance/upstream/w3c-rdf-tests/rdf/rdf11/rdf-n-triples/manifest.ttl`
    - Archive the exact RDF 1.1 N-Triples manifest inventory underlying
      the Phase 12 conformance evidence.
 6. `docs/owlapi-js/conformance/upstream/w3c-rdf-tests/rdf/rdf12/rdf-n-triples/syntax/manifest.ttl`
    - Archive the exact RDF 1.2 N-Triples syntax manifest inventory
      underlying the Phase 12 conformance evidence.
 7. `docs/owlapi-js/dependency-governance.json`
    - Document the existing private N3.js dependency boundary used for
      exact-format N-Triples tokenization.
 8. `docs/owlapi-js/migration/lessons/011-ntriples.md`
    - Capture the Phase 12 implementation decisions, evidence,
      deviations, and reusable lessons for future parser phases.
 9. `docs/owlapi-js/migration/lessons/README.md`
    - Index the N-Triples closeout lesson so later implementers can
      discover the completed phase record.
10. `docs/owlapi-js/migration/migration-status.md`
    - Mark Phase 12 complete with its conformance, differential,
      integration, performance, and governance evidence, and advance the
      next checkpoint to Phase 13.
11. `docs/owlapi-js/migration/parser-migration-playbook.md`
    - Codify the strict N-Triples migration pattern and shared RDF
      dataset-to-OWL seam for subsequent RDF syntax work.
12. `docs/owlapi-js/performance/baseline.md`
    - Add measured N-Triples parser baselines and acceptance thresholds
      so future regressions can be detected against Phase 12 evidence.
13. `docs/owlapi-js/provenance/provenance.json`
    - Record the N3.js and pinned W3C source provenance used by the
      N-Triples implementation and test corpus.
14. `src/owlapi-js/governance.test.js`
    - Enforce the new N-Triples provenance, capability, corpus, and
      dependency-governance claims as executable repository policy.
15. `src/owlapi-js/io/document.js`
    - Represent N-Triples as a distinct document format so routing and
      diagnostics preserve the caller-visible syntax identity.
16. `src/owlapi-js/manager/owlOntologyManager.js`
    - Register N-Triples with the ontology manager so direct loads and
      imported documents enter the normal parser-selection pipeline.
17. `src/owlapi-js/parser/ntriples/descriptor.js`
    - Recognize bounded absolute-IRI N-Triples inputs ahead of Turtle
      while excluding directives, XML, graph terms, and other near-match
      syntaxes.
18. `src/owlapi-js/parser/ntriples/nTriples.browser.test.js`
    - Verify the N-Triples adapter and shared RDF reconstruction path in
      the browser-compatible runtime used by the development app.
19. `src/owlapi-js/parser/ntriples/nTriples.conformance.test.js`
    - Execute all 48 positive and 51 negative pinned W3C cases to prove
      strict N-Triples conformance.
20. `src/owlapi-js/parser/ntriples/nTriples.differential.test.js`
    - Compare representative N-Triples ontology structure with the Java
      reference while documenting only intentional output differences.
21. `src/owlapi-js/parser/ntriples/nTriples.resource.test.js`
    - Guard the N-Triples parser's resource loading and dependency
      boundary against accidental eager or filesystem-specific behavior.
22. `src/owlapi-js/parser/ntriples/nTriples.test.js`
    - Cover direct loading, import closure, detection boundaries,
      diagnostics, graph normalization, and WebVOWL conversion for
      N-Triples.
23. `src/owlapi-js/parser/ntriples/parser.js`
    - Expose a strict N-Triples parser that delegates syntax events to
      the shared RDF dataset-to-OWL reconstruction pipeline.
24. `src/owlapi-js/parser/rdf/n3SyntaxAdapter.js`
    - Parameterize the private N3.js adapter with exact syntax formats
      and line-mode lexing so Turtle and N-Triples cannot silently widen
      one another.
25. `src/owlapi-js/parser/rdf/n3SyntaxAdapter.resource.test.js`
    - Verify adapter resource behavior remains lazy and portable after
      adding the N-Triples format path.
26. `src/owlapi-js/parser/rdf/n3SyntaxAdapter.test.js`
    - Prove exact-format selection, prefix handling, default-graph
      normalization, and syntax-specific diagnostics at the N3.js
      boundary.
27. `src/owlapi-js/parser/rdf/rdfSyntaxParser.js`
    - Centralize syntax-independent RDF dataset-to-OWL reconstruction so
      RDF concrete syntaxes share one tested semantic boundary.
28. `src/owlapi-js/parser/turtle/parser.js`
    - Route Turtle through the shared RDF reconstruction module without
      changing its public parser contract.
29. `src/owlapi-js/parser/turtle/turtle.test.js`
    - Protect existing Turtle behavior while its implementation adopts
      the shared RDF syntax parser seam.
30. `src/testRunnerScope.architecture.test.js`
    - Include N-Triples suites in the repository's test-runner scope
      guard so they cannot be silently omitted from normal verification.
31. `util/benchmark-owlapi-ntriples.mjs`
    - Measure N-Triples parsing and reconstruction on representative
      workloads for the Phase 12 performance baseline.
32. `util/generate-owlapi-benchmark-fixtures.js`
    - Generate the Java-reference structural fixture needed for
      reproducible N-Triples differential checks.
33. `util/generate-w3c-ntriples-fixtures.mjs`
    - Regenerate the pinned W3C N-Triples classification
      deterministically from the archived manifests and source checkout.
34. `util/owlapi-reference/fixtures/ntriples/phase12-structural.nt`
    - Provide a stable N-Triples ontology input for Java
      structural-reference generation and differential verification.
35. `util/verify-webvowl-lazy-parser-chunks.mjs`
    - Verify production builds keep RDF syntax parser dependencies lazy
      after the shared adapter and N-Triples entry point are introduced.

    canonical ontologies through RDF/JS before Phase 17 can physically
    remove the retained legacy implementation

    output only as a graph oracle with one exact, counted list-typing
    deviation

    - Mark the governed capability complete so compatibility consumers
      no longer treat the Phase 16 mapping as unavailable

    - Bind every W3C forward-mapping family and the controlled Java
      differential to executable evidence so claimed coverage cannot
      silently drift

    - Record completion of the shared translator and graph-equivalence
      gate so the implementation plan advances accurately

    - Preserve the phase decisions, acceptance evidence, performance
      findings, and Phase 17 boundary for later migration work

    - Expose the verified Phase 16 result while keeping physical legacy
      deletion blocked until this checkpoint is committed

    - Institutionalize the per-call session, exhaustive taxonomy,
      annotation patterns, and exact-differential rules needed to
      prevent future semantic regressions

    - Record environment-bound linear timing and heap evidence under the
      existing release ceiling without introducing a new threshold
 8. `docs/owlapi-js/provenance/provenance.json`
    - Trace the production mapper, inverse-reader correction, Java
      oracle, normative sources, and focused evidence to the approved
      Phase 16 work

    - Fail governance when the finite mapping inventory, structural
      taxonomy, evidence paths, or Phase 16 provenance drift apart
10. `src/owlapi-js/index.js`
    - Clarify that semantic RDF/JS mapping is available while concrete
      serialization remains deferred, preventing the package API from
      overclaiming storer support

    - Expose the completed translator from the stable RDF subpath so
      later storers can share one canonical semantic bridge

    - Protect recursive annotations and the three normative
      axiom-annotation shapes so structurally significant metadata
      survives translation

    - Protect list ordering, inverse assertions, key category order,
      n-ary individuals, and RDF 1.1 PlainLiteral conversion against

      removing exactly three non-normative Java list-type triples

    - Exercise every class-expression and data-range kind, including
      qualified cardinalities and multi-property restrictions, so model
      growth cannot bypass mapping coverage

    - Map the complete canonical ontology model through one fresh
      per-call RDF/JS session that owns blank-node identity, lists,
      graph placement, and exhaustive dispatch

    - Enforce exact linear output shapes for wide declarations, long
      collections, and deep expressions before production workloads
      depend on the mapper

    - Verify all 38 axiom kinds survive OWL-to-RDF-to-OWL reconstruction
      modulo blank-node labels and nonlogical inferred declarations

    - Lock the public export, ontology-header mapping, caller-selected
      graph placement, and stable source anonymous-individual identity

    - Classify undeclared properties through unambiguous subproperty and
      equivalence components before restriction decoding without
      fabricating declaration axioms
22. `src/testRunnerScope.architecture.test.js`
    - Keep the OWL-to-RDF differential in the default test-run inventory
      while preserving the deliberately narrow legacy exclusion
23. `util/benchmark-owlapi-owl-to-rdf.mjs`
    - Measure governed declaration, collection, and expression workloads
      with reproducible environment and package-lock identity evidence
24. `util/owlapi-reference/GenerateRdfGraph.java`
    - Generate independent graph evidence through the pinned Java OWLAPI
      public N-Triples storer without serializer-added missing types
25. `util/owlapi-reference/README.md`
    - Document reproducible oracle generation and the exact
      standards-based list-typing correction so future fixture refreshes
      retain the comparison boundary
26. `util/owlapi-reference/fixtures/rdf/phase16-graph.java.nt`
    - Retain the pinned Java graph needed to detect any unrecorded
      semantic divergence independently of triple order and blank-node
      labels
27. `util/owlapi-reference/fixtures/rdf/phase16-graph.ofn`
    - Retain the focused structural ontology that makes the Java oracle
      and JavaScript graph comparison reproducible

  - Close the remaining OWLAPI KRSS parser-surface gap before legacy
    deletion without weakening dialect separation or overstating the
    available historical corpus evidence.

File Changes:
 1. `docs/adr/0008-promote-original-krss1-into-v1.md`
    - Record the repository-owner-approved KRSS1 capability promotion,
      ambiguity policy, evidence constraints, and downstream phase
      renumbering without rewriting the earlier ADR 0002 decision
 2. `docs/adr/README.md`
    - Make the accepted KRSS1 promotion decision discoverable from the
      architecture-decision index
 3. `docs/owlapi-js/README.md`
    - Expose the completed OWL-to-RDF inventory and the new KRSS1 phase
      to contributors entering through the owlapi-js documentation
      overview
 4. `docs/owlapi-js/compatibility/capabilities.json`
    - Require KRSS1 in Phase 17 and remove its obsolete deferral so the
      machine-readable release scope cannot silently omit the parser
 5. `docs/owlapi-js/compatibility/parser-surface.md`
    - Keep the authoritative OWLAPI parser inventory aligned with
      completed KRSS2 and the required but not-yet-started KRSS1 surface
 6. `docs/owlapi-js/implementation-plan.md`
    - Define the shared-core and separate-adapter architecture, finite
      grammar probes, deterministic dialect selection, zero-corpus
      evidence classes, and complete Phase 17 acceptance gate
    - Move physical legacy deletion and package release to Phases 18 and
      19 so destructive cleanup follows the final parser checkpoint
 7. `docs/owlapi-js/migration/migration-status.md`
    - Identify original KRSS1 as the next WIP-locked migration while
      keeping the currently advertised format list honest until its
      descriptor passes the gate
 8. `docs/owlapi-js/migration/parser-migration-playbook.md`
    - Give the next implementer a current method for preserving KRSS2,
      probing KRSS1, classifying corpus evidence, and routing ambiguous
      generic KRSS input
 9. `docs/owlapi-js/provenance/provenance.json`
    - Keep live retained-file provenance aligned with Phase 18 deletion
      while preserving historical Phase 11 provenance statements
10. `src/owlapi-js/governance.test.js`
    - Enforce the required KRSS1 status, not-started progress, and Phase
      17 assignment against future governance drift
11. `src/owlapi-js/io/document.js`
    - Clarify why the KRSS1 format identity remains intentionally
      unregistered until its required Phase 17 parser passes acceptance
12. `src/owlapi-js/manager/owlOntologyManager.js`
    - Prevent the existing format identity and shared lexer from being
      mistaken for a production-ready KRSS1 descriptor
13. `src/owlapi-js/parser/krss/lexer.js`
    - Preserve the dialect-neutral lexer boundary without describing the
      newly required KRSS1 capability as permanently deferred
14. `src/owlapi-js/parser/krss2/krss2Syntax.detection.test.js`
    - Keep the KRSS2 registry-isolation test accurate during the
      interval before Phase 17 implements KRSS1

    - Keep the explicit-format failure test aligned with KRSS1 being
      required but not yet executable

message.body:
Rationale:
  - The current owlapi-js and VOWL pipeline has passed the Phase 18
    deletion gates, leaving the pre-cutover implementation
    production-unreachable and ready for physical retirement before
    native ESM packaging.

File Changes:
1. Legacy ingestion retirement (34 files)
   - Remove the production-unreachable pre-cutover parsers, converter,
     exporter, import loader, utilities, and paired characterization
     tests after the replacement and finite-reference gates passed.
   - Eliminate the competing implementation before standalone packaging
     while retaining the pinned Java oracle and current VOWL path as the
     supported comparison boundary.
2. Current runtime and differential boundaries (10 files)
   - Keep production conversion and corpus comparisons on the owlapi-js
     architecture, replace legacy import heuristics with exact catalog
     resolution, and remove old-versus-new checks that would become
     tautological after deletion.
   - Align focused VOWL expectations and bundle diagnostics with the
     retired boundary while preserving the active Java differential as
     the semantic oracle.
3. Deletion governance and test configuration (5 files)
   - Record deleted artifacts as lifecycle state instead of erasing
     their revision-bounded provenance, preserving the audit trail for
     historically reusable and reimplemented code.
   - Make physical absence, production unreachability, and default
     discovery of every active differential executable invariants, and
     remove the obsolete legacy-only test command and ignore rule.
4. Phase 18 documentation and handoff (10 files)
   - Close the deletion checklist, capture the migration lesson, and
     align the status, capability, and playbook records so Phase 19
     starts from the native ESM packaging boundary.

Rationale:
  - Avoid browser mixed-content rejection by selecting the corresponding
    HTTPS retrieval target whenever WebVOWL itself runs from an HTTPS
    page

User Experience Changes:
  - Secure deployments now attempt HTTP-declared JSON, ontology, import,
    and JSON-LD context resources through their HTTPS endpoints

File Changes:
1. `src/app/js/loadingModule.js`
   - Route direct JSON and ontology loads through secure-base URL
     resolution so HTTPS deployments do not issue requests the browser
     will block
   - Use the actual upgraded retrieval URL as the document base so
     relative ontology references resolve consistently
2. `src/app/js/loadingModule.test.js`
   - Protect direct fetch scheme selection across secure and non-secure
     bases and verify relative identifiers use the upgraded retrieval
     base
3. `src/owl2vowl/js/importResolver.js`
   - Upgrade catalog-mapped and direct import targets before fetching so
     transitive imports and remote contexts follow the same secure
     default
   - Keep diagnostics and returned document sources aligned with the
     physical URL that was requested
4. `src/owl2vowl/js/importResolver.test.js`
   - Lock the resolver mapping, fetch, and document-source contract for
     both HTTPS and HTTP WebVOWL bases
5. `src/shared/js/util/resolveFetchUrl.js`
   - Centralize the narrow HTTP-to-HTTPS rewrite so all remote loaders
     share one rule while relative and non-HTTP identifiers remain
     unchanged

Rationale:
  - Make the migration programme finite by ending it with a working
    public 1.0.1 package consumed through WebVOWL's ordinary dependency
    boundary, while moving later capabilities and external conformance
    reporting into independent follow-on plans.
  - Keep the JavaScript package recognizable to Java OWLAPI developers
    through registry-governed Java conceptual paths without exposing
    temporary WebVOWL staging seams as permanent API.

User Experience Changes:
  - No runtime behaviour changes are intended; this commit defines the
    extraction, publication, compatibility and follow-on delivery
    contracts for future implementation.

File Changes:
   1. `docs/owlapi-js/README.md`
      - Reframe owlapi-js as the historical in-tree staging name and
        identify owlapi in Hadden-Industries/owlapi as the canonical
        package and repository.
      - Link the extraction plan, standalone import-closure
        prerequisites, post-1.0 capability plan and W3C
        conformance-reporting plan from the documentation index.
      - Summarize the Phase 19 alpha and Phase 20 stable
        responsibilities, including WebVOWL's required use of public
        package specifiers.
      - Describe registry-governed Java-shaped exports, mirrored
        internal conceptual namespaces and the decision not to publish
        owlapi/rdf.
   2. `docs/owlapi-js/compatibility/standalone-import-closure-prerequisites.md`
      - Define the bounded Java-compatible model, manager, I/O, parser,
        mapping and storer capabilities needed before a self-contained
        import-closure contract can be integrated.
      - Keep those prerequisites outside the 1.0.1 completion gate while
        specifying how an external consumer composes them through public
        owlapi entry points.
   3. `docs/owlapi-js/engineering-conventions.md`
      - Distinguish temporary WebVOWL staging barrels from the future
        package's supported export surface.
      - Require standalone facades to have a Java-backed registry path
        while permitting cohesive private engines below canonical public
        definitions.
      - Record that the staging-only rdf namespace must not become a
        public package root.
   4. `docs/owlapi-js/implementation-plan.md`
      - Convert the migration document into the definitive extraction
        and publication blueprint for the standalone owlapi package.
      - Fix the npm identity and version strategy, canonical repository
        and filtered-history handoff, AGPL-3.0-only licensing, personal
        copyright and project stewardship, and inbound-equals-outbound
        contribution terms.
      - Specify the Public API Surface Registry, Java-compatible export
        roots, two-zone source layout, package metadata, bundled
        documentation, support and security contacts, runtime and
        browser support, exact dependency policy, import purity and
        zero-telemetry contract.
      - Separate Phase 19 repository extraction and 0.1.0-alpha.0
        publication under next from Phase 20 stabilization, 1.0.1
        publication under latest and WebVOWL's managed-package cutover.
      - Define deterministic tarball checks, npm staged publication,
        provenance attestations, SBOMs, checksums, immutable GitHub
        releases, correction policy and post-publication verification.
      - Harden GitHub Actions trust boundaries with pinned tools,
        Actions and runner families, a single release-manual
        environment, sole-custodian approval, explicit failure states,
        mutation-safe retries and retained release evidence.
      - Add executable completion checklists, security and packaging
        tests, performance budgets, risk controls and the research
        record supporting each settled publication decision.
   5. `docs/owlapi-js/migration/lessons/015-owl-to-rdf.md`
      - Reclassify the former src/owlapi-js/rdf barrel as a migration
        seam rather than a stable package API.
      - Place OwlToRdfTranslator under internal mapping infrastructure
        and preserve the completed Phase 16 semantics while deferring
        Java-shaped public storers to later work.
   6. `docs/owlapi-js/migration/lessons/017-legacy-deletion.md`
      - Record the signed Phase 18 completion commit and the completed
        retirement of the wired legacy pipeline.
      - Transfer the next checkpoint to Phase 19 repository extraction
        and alpha publication, with Phase 20 owning stable 1.0.1, and
        clear the superseded Git-checkpoint blocker.
   7. `docs/owlapi-js/migration/migration-status.md`
      - Record the exact Phase 18 completion hash and current repository
        baseline.
      - Add separate pending status rows for Phase 19 extraction and
        alpha publication and Phase 20 stable publication and WebVOWL
        package consumption.
   8. `docs/owlapi-js/migration/parser-migration-playbook.md`
      - Align the migration playbook with the completed Phase 18 legacy
        deletion and its signed checkpoint.
      - Define Phase 19 around repository extraction, public registry
        and API layout, and alpha publication, then assign stable 1.0.1
        and public-package consumption to Phase 20.
      - Exclude post-1.0 feature growth from the fixed ingestion and
        publication sequence.
   9. `docs/owlapi-js/post-1.0-capability-implementation-plan.md`
      - Move feature additions that are not required for the proven
        production package out of the terminal migration plan.
      - Sequence imports-closure queries, closure provision and merging,
        manager extensions, document targets and storage, Functional
        Syntax storage, strict RDF reconstruction, RDF/XML storage and
        real-consumer composition.
      - Define Java-path public API placement, cross-cutting
        verification, documentation and compatibility obligations,
        independent release gates and a separately gated TypeScript
        declaration programme.
  10. `docs/owlapi-js/w3c-test-conformance-reporting-implementation-plan.md`
      - Separate W3C implementation-report participation from the
        package's 1.0.1 release gate.
      - Define the exact installed package test subject, supported RDF
        and JSON-LD surfaces, starting evidence and pinned upstream
        suite and toolchain provenance.
      - Specify a neutral result ledger, outcome taxonomy, completeness
        accounting and EARL generation before any public conformance
        claim.
      - Lay out the phased path from local suite activation through
        exact-package execution, upstream-tool validation, retained
        evidence publication and an eventual W3C inclusion request.
      - Set transparent failure, maintenance and completion policies so
        later upstream reporting remains reproducible without blocking
        owlapi publication.

message.body:
Rationale:
  - The package implements a bounded subset of Java OWLAPI, so
    zero-major initial-development coordinates communicate its current
    maturity more accurately than a premature post-zero stability
    promise.
  - Explicit release ownership prevents conformance, cache, and
    lifecycle programmes from allocating unrelated versions or silently
    changing consumer contracts.
  - Leaving later zero-major and post-zero coordinates unassigned avoids
    speculative allocation while preserving immutable npm-history
    constraints.
  - TypeScript declarations require a separate type-design and
    maintenance decision, so the current plans permit only a separately
    authorized non-implementing exploration if demonstrated demand
    emerges.

User Experience Changes:
  - No runtime behavior changes in this documentation-only commit; the
    revised plans clarify package maturity, future capability ownership,
    and the exact releases WebVOWL should test and consume.

     - Reserve 0.1.x patches for compatible corrections, normally assign
       lifecycle capabilities to 0.2.0, and leave later coordinates
       unassigned.

       ownership, and the exploration-only TypeScript position.

docs(owlapi): Define the zero-major release roadmap

Rationale:
  - The package implements a bounded subset of Java OWLAPI, so
    zero-major initial-development coordinates communicate its current
    maturity more accurately than a premature post-zero stability
    promise.
  - Explicit release ownership prevents conformance, cache, and
    lifecycle programmes from allocating unrelated versions or silently
    changing consumer contracts.
  - Leaving later zero-major and post-zero coordinates unassigned avoids
    speculative allocation while preserving immutable npm-history
    constraints.
  - TypeScript declarations require a separate type-design and
    maintenance decision, so the current plans permit only a separately
    authorized non-implementing exploration if demonstrated demand
    emerges.

docs/owlapi-js/Deep Review of Phase 19 and Phase 20 of the owlapi Implementation Plan [2026-08-25T0020].md

message.body:
Rationale:
  - Turn the independent Phase 19 and 20 reviews and the resulting
    approved decisions into one internally consistent, executable
    blueprint before repository extraction or public package publication
    begins.
  - Prefer controls that create material evidence over ceremonial
    release steps: require a useful public alpha, make any release
    candidate conditional, and qualify the actual stable tarball against
    the complete production contract.
  - Make the single-custodian release design fail closed without
    inventing unavailable reviewers, ordinary waivers, completed
    recovery drills, or provenance claims that the selected publication
    order cannot prove.

User Experience Changes:
  - Maintainers receive an explicit path from the first public alpha to
    either an evidence-justified release candidate or a directly
    qualified stable package, with no mandatory intermediate version
    that supplies no new evidence.
  - Future consumers receive a precisely bounded native-ESM package
    through five Java OWLAPI-shaped public entry points, exact npm
    dependencies, date-pinned browser support, and WebVOWL verification
    through the same installed-package boundary.
  - This documentation-only change does not alter current WebVOWL or
    owlapi runtime behavior; it defines the implementation, publication,
    governance, and production-cutover acceptance criteria that
    subsequent work must satisfy.

File Changes:
  1. `docs/owlapi-js/Deep Review of Phase 19 and Phase 20 of the owlapi Implementation Plan [2026-08-24T1130].md`
     - Preserves the first independent deep review as durable source
       evidence for the Phase 19 and 20 critique, including its analysis
       of package extraction, public API design, release engineering,
       provenance, testing, security, governance, and WebVOWL cutover
       risks.
     - Retains the review questions and recommendations that drove the
       approved hardening decisions so future maintainers can trace the
       amended plan back to the concerns it resolves.
  2. `docs/owlapi-js/Deep Review of Phase 19 and Phase 20 of the owlapi Implementation Plan [2026-08-25T0020].md`
     - Preserves the follow-up independent review that was synthesized
       with the earlier critique before the release-plan decisions were
       finalized.
     - Records the additional cross-check of residual ambiguity and
       operational risk rather than leaving the second review as
       untracked conversation context.
  3. `docs/owlapi-js/implementation-plan.md`
     - Fixes the public identity as the unscoped npm package owlapi,
       starts the useful prerelease line at 0.1.0-alpha.0 under next,
       targets production-recommended 0.1.0 under latest, and leaves
       post-zero promotion deliberately unassigned.
     - Makes at least one useful public alpha mandatory but makes
       another alpha or 0.1.0-rc.N conditional on material
       public-validation evidence; a fully qualified and byte-frozen
       0.1.0 tarball may proceed directly from an adequate alpha.
     - Separates this plan's production publication objective from the
       later ontology-lifecycle 0.2.0 capability programme and the
       independent post-release W3C conformance-reporting programme.
     - Defines the five Java OWLAPI-recognizable public package roots,
       keeps RDF parsing and OWL-to-RDF machinery private, and makes the
       release-versioned Public API Surface Registry the compatibility
       and gap authority.
     - Specifies the history reconstruction: absorb the existing UI/UX
       branch into refactor/java-to-javascript, preserve full
       pre-rewrite identity and chronology evidence, maintain a
       schema-validated one-to-many lineage map, rebuild a clean UI/UX
       branch, and rename the fork's default branch to main without
       renaming upstream master.
     - Freezes the canonical native-ESM source/package layout, exact
       runtime and release-control dependencies, package exports, import
       purity, devEngines authority, packlist, notices, SBOM, and
       deliberate absence of TypeScript declarations or a generated
       distribution tree.
     - Requires every public version to pin its actual Baseline browser
       date and resolved data, keeps Node 22 and 24 blocking, makes Node
       26 support conditional on full LTS qualification, and proves
       bundler, import-map, local-mirror, and dedicated-worker
       consumption.
     - Requires WebVOWL to test a retained tarball in one disposable
       checkout, remove the six owlapi-owned dependencies during that
       trial, reinstall cleanly, and ultimately consume only the exact
       public registry package with no source-tree, workspace, alias, or
       legacy escape hatch.
     - Selects first-publication authority from a real npm capability
       preflight: use staged OIDC when available, otherwise use one
       bounded direct-bootstrap token path, never silently rename the
       package, and stop on a final namespace denial.
     - Defines four trust-separated workflows, exact full-SHA GitHub
       Actions, explicit hosted runners and shells, required aggregate
       checks, serialized release concurrency, bounded read retries,
       single-attempt external writes, and read-only reconciliation of
       ambiguous outcomes.
     - Binds each release to one retained tarball, staged-byte equality,
       the actual triggering workflow ref and source commit, a
       separately created signed canonical tag, validated checksums and
       CycloneDX evidence, and a fresh-cache immutable GitHub release
       verification.
     - Adds a machine-readable Phase 19 and 20 gate registry with stable
       IDs and closed applicability, permits required gates to finish
       only as PASS or validated NOT_APPLICABLE, and makes product,
       control, and external-service failures equally
       publication-blocking.
     - Keeps local Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit package checks
       mandatory while recording branded, historical, hosted, and
       real-device tests transparently as non-blocking PASS, FAIL, or
       reasoned NOT_RUN evidence; also makes performance,
       finite-resource, package-size, and bundle-size budgets explicit
       production gates.
     - Formalizes dependency audits, CodeQL and secret controls, zero
       telemetry, third-party-material governance, bounded W3C claims,
       package-name and non-affiliation review, repository privacy and
       accessibility duties, and the sole-custodian security and conduct
       model.
     - Requires checksummed encrypted off-platform backups without
       claiming a restore rehearsal and preserves a complete known-good
       WebVOWL artifact, configuration, lockfile, runbook, and
       health-check target for whole-application rollback without npm
       mutation.
     - Rewrites the Phase 19 and 20 procedures, completion criteria,
       implementation checklist, research rationale, final
       recommendation, and normative delivery diagram so the approved
       decisions remain consistent at every implementation entry point.

message.body:
Rationale:
  - Independent reviews found that Phase 19 and Phase 20 controls were
    distributed across prose, checklist rows, and evidence rules without
    one mechanically authoritative acceptance catalogue.
  - The release plan must make extraction, qualification, publication,
    and WebVOWL cutover reproducible without weakening the approved
    late-tag, staged-publication, or single-custodian model.

User Experience Changes:
  - No runtime behavior changes; this documentation update makes the
    future owlapi release process more auditable and less ambiguous for
    implementers and reviewers.

File Changes:
  1. `docs/owlapi-js/implementation-plan.md`
     - Define the requirement-authoring mechanics and make the Phase 19
       and Phase 20 catalogues authoritative, with 20 and 24 stable
       requirement IDs respectively and the implementation checklist
       treated as a derived view.
     - Divide Phase 19 into provenance, package-boundary, qualification,
       and publication-and-cutover checkpoints, and align the declared
       Node.js engine ranges with the tested Node 22.23.2 and 24.19.0
       floors.
     - Add controls for private dependency subpaths, complete locked and
       lockless browser execution, reproducible JSPM evidence,
       filtered-history zero-result commits, issue and pull-request
       references, and WebVOWL dependency ownership independent of npm
       hoisting.
     - Move namespace-support checks outside live release runs, define
       stage-loss reconciliation and byte-identical restaging,
       coordinate dist-tags with installation documentation, and state
       the audit limits of authenticated single-person approval.
     - Record the supporting architectural rationale and primary
       references so future changes can distinguish settled release
       policy from implementation detail.
